recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Handle newer, narrower Timing example or offset requests under their own Jira keys when they are in scope, rather than reopening FHIR-7912 for additional example-table design work.
issue_request: FHIR-7912 was Published/Persuasive for DSTU1 and asked for more examples showing when Timing elements are applicable, including when to use timing.event and repeat/count-style fields. The accepted resolution was to add more examples.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 5944, represented in git by a89854200640fc200f1e4ce1772e61ea11fa5610, which updated source/datatypes.html with a broader Timing criteria table including a bounds[x] column and rows such as TID for 14 days and BID starting at a specific date/time.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Timing as an active datatype, routes general datatype pages to datatypes.html, and marks Timing normative. The current combined branch preserves and extends the Timing common-use table with frequency, period, dayOfWeek, timeOfDay, when, offset, startOffset, bounds[x], and count examples. Later same-area issues FHIR-10306, FHIR-12637, and FHIR-53412 handled narrower count, event/past-event, and startOffset/endOffset work separately and do not reverse the FHIR-7912 application.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current build source already satisfies the old non-substantive request for more Timing examples; further additions would be optional example-table redesign rather than a necessary FHIR-7912 correction.
